description: A cover letter written by the AI fits on one printed page. Whenever a letter runs longer than one page, the letter's preview shows where each printed page ends, with the same marking the CV previews use and labelled in the interface language.

userStories.title: The letter preview marks where each printed page ends
userStories.description: As a user writing a cover letter, I want the preview to show where the printed page ends when my letter is longer than one page, so that I can shorten it before I print or send it.
acceptanceCriteria: A letter that prints on one page shows no marker in either preview.
A letter that prints on n > 1 pages shows exactly n − 1 markers in the editor pane and in the preview window. Marker k is labelled with page k + 1.

Each marker sits where the printed PDF's page k ends. The first and later pages are computed with their own margins, as `COVER_LETTER_PRINT_CSS` sets them, within 2 px of the unscaled preview at the fixture's content.

Each marker looks like the CV's marker: a dashed teal line across the sheet, with a constant on-screen thickness at every zoom level; the label written vertically in the gutter to the right of the sheet, never over the letter.
The label reads "Page 2" in `/fr` and `/en`, "Seite 2" in `/de` and "Pagina 2" in `/it`. It follows the interface locale, not the letter's language.
When there is no room for the label beside the sheet, the label is not drawn, the line still is, and no horizontal scroll appears. This includes the editor pane fitted to its width.
The markers follow the text as it is typed, and every zoom change, without a reload.
The marker overlay is `aria-hidden`, does not take clicks or text selection, and does not appear in the downloaded PDF or Word file.
FR-1: A letter's printed page count and page edges come from one computation, shared by both previews and by the server's one-page check.
FR-2: The printed PDF is the authority on page breaks. Whenever the computation and the PDF of a fixture disagree on the page count, the computation is wrong.
FR-3: The marker is derived state only. It is never stored, never sent to an export, and never changes the letter's layout or the preview's measured height.
FR-4: The label text is localized through the existing i18n dictionaries for fr, en, de and it. It must not be hard-coded.
FR-5: At most two AI calls are made per creation or generation: the letter, and at most one shortening.
FR-6: The shortened text is treated as untrusted AI output, exactly like the first: the same parsing, cleaning and field limits.
FR-7: Only text the AI has just written is shortened. Text the user wrote or edited is never changed.
Regression constraint: The CV page-break indicator, `computePageBreaks` and their tests are unchanged.

Regression constraint: The letter preview's zoom: fit to width, fit to page, zoom in and out, the announced level, and the scroll area that ends at the letter's last line. All of these behave as before.
Regression constraint: The letter PDF and Word output are byte-for-byte unchanged for the same letter. The export e2e and unit suites stay green.

Regression constraint: A letter that already fits on one page is created with a single AI call. Its text is produced from the new length instruction, but its fields, its company address and its 409 or AI-failure handling are unchanged.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual` keep their current results: MATCH 211 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0, and 10/10.
Verification: Unit tests for the page computation: one page, exactly one page plus or minus the tolerance, two pages and three pages; the first page's and later pages' margins; invalid heights.

Verification: Comparison with the PDF: Use letter fixtures of one, two and three printed pages. Render the real PDF through the download route. Compare its page count, and the first line of each page, with the computed edges.

Verification: Browser evidence for US-001 (e2e plus screenshots), in the editor pane and the preview window: no marker on a one-page letter; the markers on a two-page letter; the label in fr, en, de and it; the marker following typing and zoom; the label hidden in the narrow pane, with no horizontal scroll; no marker in print media.

Verification: Route tests for US-002 for both routes, through the AI test stub: fits on the first call: one call; overflows, and the shorter version fits: two calls, the shorter version is stored or returned; overflows, and the shorter version still overflows: the shorter version is kept; the shortening fails: the first version is kept; one rate-limit unit in every case; a blank letter makes no call.
Verification: An e2e test for the creation from a job application with a stubbed long letter: the stored letter prints on one page.
Verification: `ui-expert` validation of the rendered marker against the CV's marker.
Verification: `security-review` of the second AI call.
Verification: The CLAUDE.md §14 baseline, with lint at or below the tracked ceiling. Also `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual`.
FAIL condition: Wrong count: the number of markers differs from the PDF's page count minus one, for any fixture.
FAIL condition: Wrong place: a marker is more than 2 px from where the PDF's page ends.
FAIL condition: Wrong language: the label is in the letter's language instead of the interface language, or is hard-coded.
FAIL condition: Layout change: the marker changes the letter's layout, its measured height, its print output or its export.
FAIL condition: Extra cost: more than two AI calls per creation or generation, or more than one rate-limit unit.
FAIL condition: Lost content: creation or generation fails, or loses the letter, because the shortening failed or did not fit.
FAIL condition: User text changed: a stored letter, or text the user typed, is shortened.
FAIL condition: Scope: the CV indicator, the tools-page generator, translation or the exports change.
BLOCKER condition: The letter PDF cannot be rendered locally, so the page computation cannot be compared with it.

BLOCKER condition: The server cannot decide deterministically whether a letter fits on one page without a measurement it does not have, for example the font metrics of the letter's text. In that case the method must be brought back to the owner before US-002 is implemented.
Out of scope: The CV page-break indicator and its page computation.
Out of scope: The tools-page cover-letter generator (`/api/tools/generate-cover-letter`), the letter checker, and translation (`/api/cover-letters/[id]/translate`).
Out of scope: Letters already stored, and text the user types or edits: they are never shortened.
Out of scope: Any blocking, warning dialog or toast. The marker is the only signal.
Out of scope: The letter's PDF and Word export: their layout and pagination stay as they are.
Out of scope: The letter template's layout, fonts and margins.
Out of scope: Any change to the database.

userStories.title: A letter written by the AI fits on one page
userStories.description: As a user creating a cover letter from a job application, or generating one in the editor, I want the AI's letter to fit on one page, so that I do not have to cut it myself.
acceptanceCriteria: The prompt for both paths (`from-job-application` and `/api/ai/generate-cover-letter`) asks for a length that fits on one printed page, in place of the current 250–400 words.
After the first AI call, the server decides whether the letter, with its header, prints on more than one page. The decision is deterministic for a given letter.
When the letter fits, nothing else happens: there is one AI call, as today.

When it does not fit, exactly one more AI call asks for a shorter version of the same letter, in the same language, with the same structure (greeting, opening, body paragraphs, closing, sign-off). That shorter version is stored or returned instead.
When the shorter version still does not fit, it is kept as it is. Nothing is truncated, creation is not refused, and the preview's marker shows the overflow.
When the shortening call fails, or returns no usable letter, the first letter is kept. Creation and generation succeed as they would without the shortening.
The shortening call does not use another unit of the user's AI rate limit. Each creation or generation counts as one unit, as today.
A blank letter is still created blank.
The company address taken from the offer (`cover-letter-recipient-address-from-offer`) is unchanged by the shortening.
FR-1: A letter's printed page count and page edges come from one computation, shared by both previews and by the server's one-page check.
FR-2: The printed PDF is the authority on page breaks. Whenever the computation and the PDF of a fixture disagree on the page count, the computation is wrong.

FR-4: The label text is localized through the existing i18n dictionaries for fr, en, de and it. It must not be hard-coded.

FR-6: The shortened text is treated as untrusted AI output, exactly like the first: the same parsing, cleaning and field limits.
FR-7: Only text the AI has just written is shortened. Text the user wrote or edited is never changed.
